summary: Iteration 11 verification of Faz B.1 (VLC dual-engine), B.2 (Chromecast), B.4 (Downloads). Backend regression: 22/22 pytest PASS. Frontend config verification: package.json / app.json / _layout.tsx / settings.tsx / player.tsx / downloads.tsx / DownloadContext.tsx / CastButton.tsx / SmartVideoPlayer.tsx / detail.tsx all match the spec exactly (correct testIDs, correct plugin registration, correct iOS infoPlist, DownloadProvider wraps tabs, empty-state icon cloud-download-outline, TAMAMLANAN section, download-vod-btn testID, feature-downloads-btn testID present, 'Çevrimdışı Hazır' label present, CastButton with player-cast-btn testID + '• VLC' indicator in player top bar). integration_issues.issue: Bundle fails with 500 on /node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle. Root cause: `require('react-native-vlc-media-player')` inside `if (Platform.OS !== 'web') { try { require(...) } catch {} }` is still statically resolved by Metro. VLCPlayer.js does `import 'react-native/Libraries/Image/resolveAssetSource'` which is not available on web → 'Missing "./build/resolveAssetSource" specifier in "expo-asset" package'. Result: the whole Expo web preview is unusable (blank white screen). Present in 3 files: /app/frontend/app/player.tsx:31, /app/frontend/src/components/SmartVideoPlayer.tsx:24, /app/frontend/src/components/CastButton.tsx:18 (google-cast has same latent risk).

react_native_issues.issue: Static require() inside runtime Platform.OS guard is still bundled by Metro for web. VLCPlayer.js imports react-native/Libraries/Image/resolveAssetSource which has no web export. Fix: extract the require into a platform-specific module, e.g. create /app/frontend/src/native/vlc.ts (native only) and /app/frontend/src/native/vlc.web.ts (returns null), then `import { VLCPlayer } from '@/src/native/vlc'`. Metro's platform resolver will pick the correct file. Reference: /app/frontend/app/player.tsx:29-32, /app/frontend/src/components/SmartVideoPlayer.tsx:22-25.

Same anti-pattern as VLC — `require('react-native-google-cast')` inside Platform.OS check. Not currently triggering an error in the log (likely because bundling fails on VLC first), but will exhibit the same failure once VLC is fixed. Apply same platform-specific wrapper pattern. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/CastButton.tsx:16-22.

rca_of_issue: Metro's static bundler traverses every `require('module-name')` call regardless of surrounding runtime conditions (Platform.OS check, try/catch). react-native-vlc-media-player's entry chain imports 'react-native/Libraries/Image/resolveAssetSource', which react-native-web maps to 'expo-asset/build/resolveAssetSource' — a specifier that no longer exists in current expo-asset. Result: bundling for `platform=web` fails with 'Missing "./build/resolveAssetSource" specifier in "expo-asset" package', HTTP 500 on entry.bundle, blank screen. Reproduction: `curl http://localhost:3000` returns HTML, but `curl 'http://localhost:3000/node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle?platform=web'` returns 500. Fix: replace the inline `require()` with a platform-suffixed module (e.g. `src/native/vlc.ts` on native, `src/native/vlc.web.ts` returning null on web) so Metro's platform resolver excludes VLC from the web bundle entirely. Same fix required for CastButton to prevent regression once VLC is fixed.
